bull_case.thesis: SNGP is a regulated gas utility trading at a steep discount to its own earnings power, with a composite fair value 33.7% above the current price and a dividend track record that keeps paying even as the stock sells off. The setup rewards patience through a macro-driven dip rather than a company-specific breakdown.
pillars: P/E of 4.43 sits in the cheapest third of PSX names on EPS of Rs22.95
Composite fair value of 135.96 vs price of 101.72 implies 33.7% upside (undervalued verdict)
Two dividends paid in the last year (75% and 30% payouts) with a moderate 45.47% payout ratio leaves room without straining coverage
Beta of 0.31 means the stock historically moves far less than the broader market, damping the current risk-off shock
Avg daily traded value of Rs419.2M gives ample liquidity for clean entry sizing
bull_case.best_evidence: Composite fair value of 135.96 against a 101.72 price (33.7% undervalued) anchored by earnings-power (146.27) and Graham (159.81) methods.
bull_case.what_would_break_it: If Brent crude's move above $92/bbl (impact-4 news, 2026-07-20 and 07-22) feeds into cost pressure that erodes the already-thin ~1% net margin, or if price breaks decisively below the SMA50 (106.8) confirming the downtrend, the cheap-valuation thesis loses its earnings anchor.

bear_case.thesis: SNGP is in a confirmed technical downtrend — down 17.21% in 20 sessions and below both its SMA20 and SMA50 — arriving at the same moment oil-driven macro risk-off is hitting the whole exchange, and the 'undervalued' fundamental read rests on a composite that hides sharp internal disagreement. This is a falling-knife setup dressed as a value trade.
pillars: Price down 3.03% today and 17.21% over 20 sessions, below SMA20 (113.73) and SMA50 (106.8), RSI14 at 37.6 and falling
No defined support level in the TA memo (support: null) — downside has no technical floor
Net margin only ~1.2% (Rs14.55B net income on Rs1.24T revenue) — a thin, cost-plus cushion vulnerable to input-cost swings
Brent crude above $92/bbl (impact-4, 2026-07-22) plus a broad KSE-100 slide of 1,703.64 points same day — sector and index headwinds are live, not hypothetical
The four valuation methods diverge wildly: DDM at just 24.44 vs Graham at 159.81 — a nearly 6x spread
bear_case.attack_on_bull: The bull's best evidence — the 33.7% undervalued composite — is also the weakest pillar. It averages four methods that disagree by as much as 6x (DDM 24.44 vs Graham 159.81). The DDM, which values SNGP purely on its actual cash dividend stream, says the stock is worth a quarter of its current price. Blending that into a single 'undervalued' headline number hides a real possibility that the market is correctly pricing thin, regulated cash flows, not mispricing a cheap earner.
bear_case.worst_case: Continued oil-driven risk-off (Brent already above $92, KSE-100 down 1,703.64 points same session) extends the 17.21% 20-day decline through the SMA50 (106.8) with no defined support below it; if Brent-driven cost pressure compresses net margin below the current ~1.2%, the DDM read of 24.44 — less than a quarter of the 101.72 price — becomes the more credible fair-value anchor rather than the 135.96 composite.
